title: Verification result
description: Output of the independent onchain verifier. D-006: direct and x402 execution pass the SAME verifier and produce this same shape. It is computed only from chain reads; nothing a provider asserts may appear as an input. A provider success response that this verifier contradicts yields E_PROVIDER_RESPONSE_UNTRUSTED.

allOf.$comment: A verified outcome cannot coexist with a drifted registry or with single-sourced/disagreeing RPC evidence. Previously these were prose; ajv ignores $comment, so they are now real constraints.
A custodial job cannot be verified until custody has actually been handed over.

Custody evidence is REQUIRED for any verified outcome, not merely constrained when present. Previously the custody guard only fired if custody already existed, so deleting the key let a provider-custody-transfer-last job report verified while never proving the name left provider custody. For direct and sponsored-to-owner this is trivial to populate: mode, transferRequired false, transferCompleted true.

outcome.description: partial means the ENS postconditions hold and a requested identity postcondition does not. It is a real outcome, not a failure: ENS completion and identity completion are separated so recovery never repeats paid or irreversible work.

canonicality.description: Re-checked at verification time, not inherited from the plan. A drifted registry invalidates the whole result.

forwardAddress.description: Address the name forward-resolves to THROUGH the Universal Resolver. A registered name with a zero resolver is not a usable identity and does not satisfy the postcondition.

currentTokenId.description: Read at verification time. It is mutable and may differ from the value observed at binding time.

reverseRecordSet.description: Optional follow-up. Never required for registration success (D-003 scope).

identity.description: Present when identity was requested. Absent when identity is none.

boundTokenId.description: Token ID observed at binding time. Gate: P-005. Informational once a resource anchor is in use, since the token ID is expected to change.

boundTokenIdIsCurrent.description: Gate: P-005. Meaningful only for a token-id anchor. False is TERMINAL: there is no unbind, so recovery means minting a fresh agent (E_IDENTITY_BINDING_ORPHANED), not resuming. Under a resource anchor this is expected to go false harmlessly after a role change, which is precisely why the resource anchor was adopted.

controlVerified.description: The expected owner still controls the ERC-8004 identity right now.

kind.description: Which anchor the binding uses. resource is the accepted design (D-009); token-id and labelhash are recorded so an existing non-conforming binding can still be described and flagged.

invariantUnderTokenIdChange.description: True for resource. False for token-id.

survivesReregistration.description: MUST be false for a safe anchor. True means the anchor would follow a stranger who re-registers the name after expiry, inheriting this identity.

epochEqualityChecked.description: Whether the verifier re-read getResource(storedAnchor) and required it to equal the stored value. This single check fails closed on both expiry and re-registration.

bindingMetadataAddress.description: The 20-byte value read from the ERC-8004 registry's reserved agent-binding metadata key (ERC-8217 discovery). Read via getMetadata(agentId, 'agent-binding').

bindingMetadataMatches.description: Whether bindingMetadataAddress equals adapterProxy. A stale or foreign value means the identity is discoverable as pointing at a DIFFERENT binding contract, which is a real failure rather than an advisory, so this is required whenever bound is true.

ownerCheckMethod.description: Which accessor established live ownership. getOwner is absent on older registries; ownerOf(getTokenId(anyId)) is equivalent and universally available.

allOf.$comment: A claimed binding must say which standard it used, prove the ERC-8217 discovery pointer resolves back to this adapter, and name its anchor. Without all three, bound:true is an unfalsifiable assertion.

D-009. An anchor that survives re-registration is the capture scenario the decision exists to prevent: it follows whoever re-registers the name after expiry and hands them the previous holder's identity. The field's own description said MUST be false; that is now enforced rather than described.

D-009 verification is epoch equality, not a bare read: re-read getResource(storedAnchor) and require it to equal the stored value. A resource anchor claimed without that re-read is exactly the distinction the decision draws, so bound cannot be asserted without it.

checks.description: Itemised evidence. Each check reports expected and actual, so a failure is diagnosable without re-running the verifier.

evidenceSource.description: How the reads were obtained. Two independent endpoints are consulted so a single equivocating RPC cannot manufacture a passing result (gap E9).

rpcEndpointCount.description: At least two independent endpoints, so a single equivocating RPC cannot manufacture a passing result. The bound matches the requirement instead of merely describing it.

providerAssertionsUsed.description: Structurally pinned to false. If a verifier ever needs to record that it used a provider assertion, that is a schema change and a decision, not a runtime option.

transferRequired.description: True exactly when mode is provider-custody-transfer-last.

transferCompleted.description: Whether the name actually left provider custody and reached the intended owner.

interimHolder.description: Who held the name during the custody window.

custody.description: Custody completion. WS03 requires custody to be explicit in both the signed intent and the final verification. Without this a provider-custody-transfer-last job could pass every other check while quietly never completing the transfer.

allOf.$comment: transferRequired is derived from the mode, not asserted independently. A custodial mode that claims no transfer is required is self-contradictory.
Neither mode ever places the name in provider custody, so neither can require a transfer out of it.
